prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a grocery aisle layout with multi-tiered shelves angled from the far left (1.0–1.5 m away) toward the near right (0.4–0.6 m away), while the foreground contains a person's right hand and a held purple gnocchi box at 0.2–0.4 m. Across frames 1 to 3, the camera wearer approaches and angles slightly right toward the shelves before turning left in frames 4 and 5, which brings a shopping basket and a left hand at 0.3–0.4 m into the lower-left foreground while the distant aisle background drops off beyond 3 m in dark tones. Nearly all middle- and upper-shelf items (boxes, dressing bottles, and canisters spaced 0.1–0.3 m apart vertically and horizontally) are within arm's reach (under 0.8 m) in frames 1 to 4, while the held box in the lower foreground partially occludes the lower shelf and the bottles directly behind it, and all heads and torsos remain completely out of view. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the receding depth gradient along the shelf rows and the step-change between the held box and the shelf behind it, even where packaging textures are busy or motion-blurred in frame 4. However, the map is unreliable along the top shelf ledge in frames 1 to 4, where the bright white shelf lip and canisters appear overly bright (nearer than the hands at 0.2 m) due to relative depth scaling and surface reflectance artifacts.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map partitions the scene into foreground hands (labeled 'person' at 0.2–0.4 m in the lower right, joined by a second hand on the lower left in frame 5), the held rectangular box at 0.3 m (mislabeled 'book' or unmarked), and individual shelf containers 0.4–1.0 m away above and behind the held box. Across the 5 frames, as the held box rotates to show its back in frames 2–3 and front again in frames 4–5 while moving left toward the basket (0.1–0.2 m between the two hands in frame 5), the masks track the foreground hand overlapping the top-right edge of the box and the box occluding the lower-middle shelf. Unlike the RGB image, the segmentation map explicitly isolates discrete object boundaries for tightly packed bottles standing side-by-side (0.05–0.1 m apart) on the middle shelf and separates the foreground hands from the cluttered grocery background. However, its semantic labels and mask boundaries are highly unreliable: the entire shelving unit is misclassified as a single 'refrigerator' mask in frames 1, 2, 3, and 4, the yellow mustard bottles on the right are mislabeled 'banana' in frames 2 and 4, the gnocchi boxes are labeled 'book' or 'cake', and a background bottle neck is mislabeled 'person' in frames 2 and 4. Furthermore, in frame 5, the background shelves and distant aisle (>1.5 m away) drop out completely into unsegmented black background, leaving only the foreground hands, held box, and two nearby dressing bottles on the right.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only a single magenta right-hand skeleton in the lower-center-right foreground (at roughly 0.2–0.4 m from the camera wearer) during frames 1, 2, and 3, with no yellow body keypoints anywhere because the camera wearer's torso and head (and any other person's body) are out of the field of view. In frames 1 to 3, the tracked right hand is positioned within arm's reach just in front of and below the middle shelf, with its wrist on the right and fingers extending leftward over the top edge of the held box as the hand tilts and rotates the box. Compared to the RGB strip, the 21-joint hand skeleton explicitly resolves the 3D-projected finger articulation, knuckle spacing, and palm orientation against the top of the box despite partial self-occlusion of the lower fingers. However, the pose map is completely unreliable in frames 4 and 5, where it fails to detect both the right hand on the right side of the box and the left hand entering from the lower left at 0.3–0.4 m (likely due to motion blur and cropping at the frame borders), and it provides no spatial information about the shelves, objects, or viewing direction of any person.
